trial_court: learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kapurthala (FIR No.03 dated 25.07.2015)
case_name: Gurmukh Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab and another (wife, police station)

facts_of_case: The parties were in a matrimonial discord. A compromise was arrived at between the parties and FIR No.03 dated 25.07.2015 under Sections 406/498A IPC was quashed. The petitioner was declared a proclaimed person vide order dated 22.01.2016, which was contrary to law.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to quash a criminal proceeding to demonstrate that the compromise is genuine and arrived at without any pressure, coercion or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: Satisfaction is expressed that the settlement arrived at between the parties is genuine, arrived at out of their own free will without any pressure.

legal_principles.principle: A settlement arrived at between parties in a matrimonial dispute must be genuine and not the result of any pressure, coercion or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: Respondent No.2 stated that she has compromised the matter with the accused petitioner out of her own free will, without any pressure or coercion.

outcome.final_order: The FIR No.03 dated 25.07.2015 under Sections 406/498A IPC and all consequential proceedings were quashed.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
